messages.subject: text on my ggplot
parts:

Error: unexpected ')' in:
"x = Hu_IL_6__19_, y = 3, size = 5,
colour = "black"))"
 


p7<-ggplot2.dotplot(data=cyt, xName='cat_con',yName='Hu_IL_6__19_',
                axisLine=c(1,"solid","darkblue"),
                addBoxplot=TRUE,notch=TRUE,
                xtitle="PCR Result", ytitle="Hu_IL_6__19_",
                mainTitle="PCR Result by Hu_IL_6__19_",
                mainTitleFont=c(14,"bold.italic", "black"),
                xtitleFont=c(14,"bold", "#993334"),
                ytitleFont=c(14,"bold", "#993334"))

p7+annotate("text", label = "Footnote",
            x = Hu_IL_6__19_, y = 3, size = 5,
            colour = "black"))

messages.author: 0c39e60ddb38622b
messages.subject: Re: text on my ggplot
parts:
Roman, I don't think it's the closing paren of the call that produces p7, but rather what x = Hu_IL_6__19_ is supposed to represent in the annotate() call. Consider the following reproducible example:

DF <- data.frame(x = 1:3, y = 1:3, lab = LETTERS[1:3])

library(ggplot2)

# Error
ggplot(DF, aes(x = x, y = y)) + geom_point() +
    annotate(geom = "text", x = x , y = 0.5, label = lab)

# Works
ggplot(DF, aes(x = x, y = y)) + geom_point() +
    annotate(geom = "text", x = DF$x, y = 0.5, label = DF$lab)

annotate() does not allow mappings via aes(), but it does allow one to pass in vector arguments. However, those vectors need to be 'visible' to ggplot() from the calling environment of the function. I think if the OP uses cyt$ Hu_IL_6__19_ in the annotate() call it will work, but that cannot be independently verified in the absence of the data frame cyt. Until then, your guess is as good as mine...

Dennis
